answer: A threshold coin flipping protocol lets a group jointly flip a fair coin, and the spiral of the design is that each participant commits to a random bit before any reveal. The mesa of the protocol is that the outcome is the XOR of all committed bits, so a single cheater cannot bias it. A Sybil cannot control the flip because it would need to corrupt a threshold of participants, and the nebula of the commitment phase makes every bit binding before the result is known.
